title: Joe Kent, a Top Counterterrorism Official for the Trump Administration, Resigns, Citing Iran War
partialText: Mr. Kent is the highest-ranking Trump administration official to quit in opposition to the conflict. He said pressure from Israel had pushed the president into war against Iran.

title: Israel’s Killing of Ali Larijani Could Allow Military to Tighten Grip on Iran
partialText: As Iran’s top national security official, Mr. Larijani had a reputation for acting as a bridge between hard-line figures in the armed forces and more moderate political factions.

title: Dozens Dead in Pakistani Airstrike on Kabul
partialText: The attack hit a drug rehabilitation facility, and Afghanistan vowed to retaliate, risking an escalation of the conflict between the two countries.

title: Why Are Pakistan and Afghanistan Fighting?

title: What’s in Trump’s SAVE Act, the Voter ID Bill Republicans Are Pushing?
partialText: The legislation would require voters to prove their citizenship in person upon registration, ban IDs without a photo at polling places and criminalize failures to enforce such requirements.

title: M.T.A. Sues Trump Administration to Release 2nd Avenue Subway Funding
partialText: New York transit officials are seeking nearly $60 million in overdue federal funding to extend the subway line to East Harlem. The administration’s rationale for the freeze has been inconsistent.

title: In Rural New York, Some See Proposed A.I. Center as a Needless Intrusion
partialText: The data center, to be built between Buffalo and Rochester, will raise electric bills and harm a nearby tribal reservation, opponents argue. “I can’t think of one good reason for it,” a local resident said.

title: Why March Weather Is Weird: Snow, Tornadoes, Recording-Breaking Heat and More
partialText: Snow, tornadoes, record-breaking heat, a dust storm — and that’s just last weekend. Here’s how to understand what’s going on, and the role climate change is playing in all of it.
